headline: Across 10 cohorts, the one-eye student's AUROC gained +0.024 on average (8 of 10 improved), whereas this card's split shows -0.010.
idea: A model trained on both eyes can teach a model that sees only one eye.
The student copies the teacher's internal representation, not only its answers.
At deployment only one eye image is needed.
findings: On the detailed split (left eye, AMD preset) AUROC went from 0.711 to 0.702, difference -0.010 [95% CI -0.033, +0.012]. The two-eye teacher reached 0.729. The paper reports AMD left 0.931 (0.846–0.984) → 0.966 (0.936–0.987); this split does not reproduce that gain. ΔCKA +0.118; linear probe 0.718 → 0.706.

Across 10 cohorts the mean Δ AUROC is +0.024 (SD 0.021), positive in 8 of 10. Across cohorts Δ precision runs from -0.113 to +0.158 and Δ FPR from -0.071 to +0.070, so the sign of the threshold trade-off depends on the split. In the sweep, Δ AUROC peaks at +0.049 near inter-eye correlation 0.4 (α 0.1) and is +0.014 at 0.95 (α 0.1).

try_next.label: Eyes nearly identical
try_next.why: The sweep shows the gain falling to +0.014 at inter-eye correlation 0.95; this checks whether a second eye that agrees with the first adds less.

try_next.label: Noisy deployment eye, clean privileged eye
try_next.why: The left eye is noisier at inference while the teacher gets a cleaner right eye; tests whether the privileged eye helps more when the deployed image is poor.

try_next.label: Common disease (DR preset)
try_next.why: Same settings with 30% prevalence; compares the detailed-split gain and the FPR and precision trade-off with AMD.

caveats: Toy simulation of 128-d synthetic eye features, not ODIR images or RETFound-Green; magnitudes are not comparable to the paper.
Sweep is an extension not in the paper, two cohorts per cell; α is on this toy's scale.
